Some of these lubricants will be introduced unintentionally into the drill hole with the pipe although excess lubricant will be wiped off. It is unlikely that detectable amounts will reach the water column or the bottom sediments. If these materials do reach the water column or bottom sediments they will be detected by the chemical studies associated with the studies of the water and sediments. Drillers will be instructed to keep the use of these lubricants to a minimum.
13. <u>Drilling and Blasting</u>. The actual drilling of a hole through the RIS will cause a local change in the physical characteristic of the ice mass, and the sediments and bedrock. Should blasting be chosen as the method of penetrating the last few meters through the ice shelf, the shock wave may have a considerable temporary effect on the local biota, if such are found to exist. Due to the damping effect of the water column, it is unlikely that blasting would contribute anything but a minor environmental impact.
14. <u>Trenching (Snow Stratigraphy</u>). Shallow pits will be dug in order to study snow stratigraphy. These will be filled by new and drifting snow before the end of the season.
15. Explosives (Geophysical Survey). The detonation of explosives for the seismic investigation of the RIS, the water column and possibly the sediments beneath may impose a local impact on the environment. The quality of the atmosphere will be affected by the release of particulate matter.
